issue_context.title: Add a metric tracking pod priorities used in a cluster
issue_context.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
A histogram that tracks the priorities used in a cluster.

**Why is this needed**:
Helps platform operators track feature usage. Priorities in particular are important since they trigger preemption in the scheduler, and so understanding how they are used helps inform optimizations related to preemption.

/sig scheduling

review_comments: this should come after the klog.V(3) statement that announces that we're attempting to schedule this pod
do we want to record the priority for the same pod if it goes through multiple attempts in multiple scheduling cycles? that seems counter-intuitive.

this would create buckets [1, 2), [2, 4), [4, 8)..., [16k, inf), right? In practice, I've seen pod priorities to be usually in the 1000s, which wouldn't give this much granularity (e.g. priority 5000 and 6000 cannot be differentiated). Also, would this capture pod priority 0 (default value)?
Yes, I think in this case defining buckets manually is probably most reasonable. Exponential buckets are really meant for buckets of request latencies of a network service.

while I don't have any strong opinions on whether this should be a new metric on its own, perhaps we could explore the possibility of adding pod priority as a label to existing metrics such as `pod_scheduling_attempts` or `pod_scheduling_duration_seconds`. However, one concern will be the high cardinality of pod priorities.
Thinking a bit more on this I think a counter metrics to keep count of how many pods have priority>0 maybe more useful..what's your thoughts @ahg-g ?
I fear that adding pod priority to existing metrics would make the cardinality explode. I think having this separate metric makes sense.
